items.title: England's Brook hits record ODI double ton but Sri Lanka pull off epic chase in Rawalpindi clash
items.description:
England’s Harry Brook smashed the fastest double-century in One-Day International (ODI) history and became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format but Sri Lanka sealed a two-wicket win in their tri-series clash with one ball to spare in Rawalpindi on Thursday.
The 27-year-old captain rewrote the record books by racing to his double hundred in 114 balls, surpassing the previous mark of 117 deliveries set by India’s Shubman Gill.

items.title: China orders 'all-out' rescue after Tibet quake kills 16
items.description:
China ordered an “all-out” rescue effort in Tibet on Friday after an earthquake killed at least 16 people, injured dozens and flattened hundreds of homes, state media reported.
Footage showed rescue workers with torches clambering in the dark through some of the more than 300 houses that Xinhua said collapsed in the 7.0-magnitude quake on Thursday evening.
Diners ran out of restaurants and items fell off wobbling supermarket shelves as the tremor struck, according to clips on state broadcaster CCTV, which said 65 people were injured.

items.title: PCB opens direct signings window for PSL teams, announces pre-season roadmap
items.description:
The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Friday opened the direct signings window for all eight HBL Pakistan Super League (PSL) franchises and unveiled the pre-season roadmap for the 12th edition of the tournament, which will be held from March 18 to May 2 next year.
The player-movement cycle has begun with immediate effect, with the Player Auction scheduled for Jan 23 next year.

items.title: 'Generational rage': Young Europeans fight to be heard
items.description:
From blockaded schools in Rome to tent camps in Madrid and street protests in France, young people across Europe are turning their anger on a political class they say is not listening.
Their demands vary, but they are united in wanting to make their often marginalised voices heard, sometimes even with radical methods in the face of heavy-handed policing.

items.title: Landslide leaves thousands stranded on Baltistan Road
items.description:
Passengers cross a road blocked by boulders in the Shangus area of Skardu’s Roundu Valley.—Dawn
			
			

• GBDMA warns against travel as road to remain closed
• Residents call for safety measures on thoroughfare             

GILGIT: The Baltistan Road was blocked by landslides near Shangus in Skardu’s Roundu Valley on Thursday morning, leaving thousands of passengers, including tourists, stranded on both sides.

Local residents have expressed concern over the failure to implement safety measures on the road, which is frequently blocked by landslides and has witnessed numerous fatal accidents.
